waterbody.name: Pampanga estuary
waterbody.anchorMeaning: The article's study-area anchor only; not a sampling-station coordinate, occurrence coordinate or boundary.
waterbody.sourceReportedExtent: Approximately 6.8 km using surface/mid-water salinity and 16 km using bottom salinity during reconnaissance.
waterbody.administrativeCrosswalk: The article describes a downstream Pampanga River estuary bounded by Manila Bay and the freshwater river. It does not provide station coordinates or establish overlap with the Sasmuan Pampanga Coastal Wetlands Ramsar polygon, Batang Dos, or Minalin Channel.

decision: Retain this as a historical, gear- and season-bounded Pampanga estuary study. Preserve the author-reported table labels for research and taxonomy follow-up only. Do not present them as current occurrences, a whole-estuary checklist, Sasmuan Ramsar-site records, or public app assertions; item-level reuse terms conflict and remain unresolved.

sources.title: Fish communities and environmental variables during dry season in Pampanga estuary (Philippines)

accessReview.repositoryExtractedText: HTTP 200; full article text was read in memory for this review. No full-text copy was saved to the repository.
accessReview.tableReviewed: Table 1 in the repository's extracted full text
accessReview.stationData: The article describes nine stations and shows their positions on a map, but the reviewed text gives no per-station coordinates. No coordinates were digitized from the figure.
accessReview.rightsConflict: The article text states © 2020 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved; Crossref exposes text-and-data-mining license records, not a clear item-specific table-reuse license. The institutional CC BY metadata conflicts with those signals and was not independently authenticated. Treat reuse for a public app as unverified pending rights-holder clarification.
accessReview.reuseDisposition: Research-only factual review with attribution; public reuse permission is unresolved, and no table, figure, article prose or data has been added to the app.

sources.title: RIS for Site no. 2445, Sasmuan Pampanga Coastal Wetlands, Philippines
sources.roleInReview: Compared only to determine whether the estuary study stations could be assigned to the Ramsar site. The study article does not supply station coordinates or a polygon crosswalk, so no spatial overlap was established.

studyDesign.gear: Otter trawl; the method describes ten minutes of operation per station at approximately 1.84 knots.
limitations: The study covers one dry season in April 2010, not the full annual cycle.
Four of 36 planned trawl samples were not completed because of bad weather and net entanglement.
Catch composition is specific to the study gear and sampling protocol.
The paper reports an estimated estuary boundary; its figure is not a validated boundary dataset.

sourceReportedResults.reportedTaxaMeaning: Author-reported count for this historical study, not a current checklist or population estimate.

table1AuthorReportedTaxonLabels.label: Oxyurichthys opthalmonema
table1AuthorReportedTaxonLabels.note: Source spelling preserved; no nomenclatural correction performed.

taxonomyAndLocalityReview.estuaryToSasmuanHydrologicConnectionInte: The sources describe related Pampanga River/coastal-delta settings, but a waterbody or boundary intersection cannot be asserted from the available station data. Keep records separated.

nextStep: Continue with independently sourced Pampanga River reaches outside this 2010 estuary study and verify station-level site identities from distinct primary sources. Preserve each river reach, lake, wetland and estuary separately; Central Luzon remains incomplete.
